nodes.label: ISO 19123 Schema for coverage geometry and functions
nodes.norm_label: iso 19123 schema for coverage geometry and functions

nodes.label: Discrete coverage
nodes.rationale: Chosen as the representation of classification results because it returns the same attribute values for every direct position within a single spatial object; geometry can be polygons, grid cells, points or curves.

nodes.label: Discrete surface coverage
nodes.rationale: Required when the coverage range partitions an area; uses GM_Surface geometry per ISO 19123:2005 6.8. Natural phenomena tend to irregular polygons; sensor data tend to grid tessellations.

nodes.norm_label: annex b a priori and a posteriori classification systems

nodes.label: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
nodes.norm_label: food and agriculture organization of the united nations (fao)

nodes.label: Sustainable Development Goals and global reporting frameworks (Rio Conventions, Paris Agreement, Sendai Framework, 2030 Agenda)
nodes.norm_label: sustainable development goals and global reporting frameworks (rio conventions, paris agreement, sendai framework, 2030 agenda)

nodes.label: ISO 19144 series Geographic information - Classification systems
nodes.norm_label: iso 19144 series geographic information - classification systems
nodes.rationale: Jointly developed by FAO and ISO/TC211 to provide a flexible foundation for land cover/land use classification and support SDG and international reporting obligations.

nodes.label: Land Cover Classification System (LCCS)
nodes.rationale: FAO LCCS v1 (2000) and v2 (2005) by Di Gregorio are the source of the a priori / a posteriori / legend definitions used in the standard.

nodes.label: A posteriori classification
nodes.rationale: Classes defined after clustering field samples. Advantage: flexibility and minimal generalization, fits local data. Disadvantage: cannot define standardized classes and hampers comparison; but standardized rules for establishing classes can be defined.

nodes.label: A priori classification
nodes.rationale: Classes defined before data collection as abstract conceptualizations. Advantage: standardized classes independent of area and means. Disadvantage: rigid; field samples may not fit predefined classes.

nodes.label: Classification system
nodes.rationale: System for assigning objects to classes; consists of a set of classifiers. Shall be scale independent and source independent so classes apply at any scale or level of detail regardless of collection means (§5.2). No single system serves all application areas, hence a common structure plus registers.

nodes.label: Hierarchical classification system
nodes.rationale: Classes at each level must be mutually exclusive and criteria must not be repeated across levels. Most systems are hierarchical because this gives greater consistency: broad classes with few diagnostic criteria at top, more criteria at lower levels.

nodes.label: Mutual exclusivity of classes
nodes.rationale: Classifiers must be defined so classes at a level are mutually exclusive, ensuring unambiguous assignment.

nodes.label: Non-hierarchical classification system
nodes.rationale: All classes mutually exclusive; applies to a single level of information (single scale or type).

nodes.label: CL_ClassificationLegendItem
nodes.rationale: Adds code and alphaCode to RE_RegisterItem: a code is an information-process-efficient denotation for data interchange outside the register, distinct from the itemIdentifier used inside the register.

nodes.label: CL_ClassificationRegister
nodes.rationale: Subclass of RE_Register adding scopeSet, fieldOfApplicationSet and functionalLanguage; ISO 19110 elements are reused to describe the register to keep a parallelism between feature descriptions and classifier descriptions.

nodes.label: A.3 Conformance of a register of classifiers
nodes.norm_label: a.3 conformance of a register of classifiers

nodes.label: Classification rule
nodes.rationale: Rules relate classified objects via hierarchy, classifier relationships, or spatial/scale aspects (e.g. dominance in Savannah, minimum area). Simple schemes can describe rules in text; complex schemes need machine-processable form, hence functionalLanguage attribute.

nodes.label: Cross-referencing between classifier registers
nodes.rationale: Compatible register structures across information communities allow conversion or fusion of data between classification systems.

nodes.label: Mixed classification (A|B)
nodes.rationale: When an object is below minimal area at a scale, a mixed class A|B with A dominant and B above a threshold is created so the material's existence is still shown.

nodes.label: Management of classifiers through registration
nodes.rationale: Classifiers are registered per ISO 19135 because sets need extension and modification over time; structure and schema can be standardized while specific classifier details live in the register, enabling many classifiers, community maintenance, and cross-referencing between registers of different information communities.

nodes.label: Technical standard
nodes.rationale: ISO 19135 requires a technical standard to define item classes in a conformant register; ISO 19144-1 serves as that technical standard for registers of classifiers.

nodes.label: Concept dictionary register for a classification scheme
nodes.norm_label: concept dictionary register for a classification scheme

nodes.label: ISO 19126 Feature concept dictionaries and registers
nodes.norm_label: iso 19126 feature concept dictionaries and registers

nodes.label: CL two-letter UML prefix convention
nodes.rationale: UML class names carry a two-letter prefix identifying the source standard and package (CL for ISO 19144-1) per ISO 19100 series convention; Table 1 lists CV, DS, GF, GM, MD, MI, RE, SC, TM.

nodes.label: Classification
nodes.rationale: Abstract representation of real-world phenomena using classifiers; a systematic framework of class names, definitions and relations. Class boundaries must be clear and based on objective criteria.

nodes.label: Classifier
nodes.rationale: Definition used to assign objects to legend classes; may be algorithmic or rule-based. Classifiers are application-area dependent and registered so the set can be extended and maintained over time.

nodes.label: Legend
nodes.rationale: Application of a classification in a specific area at a defined mapping scale with a specific data set; a subset of classifiers. Shall be scale dependent and source dependent because real data imposes scale/source limits. Analogous to a feature catalogue subset of a feature concept dictionary.

nodes.label: Legend class
nodes.rationale: Class resulting from a classification process. Term 'legend class' chosen to avoid confusion with 'class' in UML and 'item class' in registration.

nodes.label: Scale independence and source independence
nodes.rationale: Classification systems must be scale and source independent so classes are applicable at any scale and regardless of collection means; legends are where scale/source limits enter.

nodes.label: ISO 19115-2 Metadata - Extensions for imagery and gridded data
nodes.norm_label: iso 19115-2 metadata - extensions for imagery and gridded data

nodes.label: ISO/TS 19129 Imagery, gridded and coverage data framework
nodes.norm_label: iso/ts 19129 imagery, gridded and coverage data framework

nodes.label: ISO 19144-1:2009 Classification System Structure
nodes.rationale: First part of ISO 19144 series; defines the common structure of geographic classification systems and the register mechanism for classifiers, so that subsequent parts can standardize specific application-area systems (LCML, LUML). Based on FAO LCCS publications.

nodes.label: Soil Map of the World / USDA Soil Taxonomy
nodes.norm_label: soil map of the world / usda soil taxonomy

nodes.label: functionalLanguage attribute
nodes.rationale: Specifies the notational system (e.g. Prolog) for formal rule definitions; mandatory where rules are specified so rules can be processed automatically.

nodes.label: A.2 Conformance of a classification system
nodes.norm_label: a.2 conformance of a classification system

nodes.label: ISO 19109:2005 Rules for application schema (General Feature Model)
nodes.norm_label: iso 19109:2005 rules for application schema (general feature model)

nodes.label: Classified object
nodes.rationale: Spatial/temporal/spatiotemporal object assigned to a legend class. Classified objects are features but not atomic: they are related to each other by the classifiers that decompose the whole (top-down), unlike conventional features which are atomic units assembled bottom-up.
